source_records.source_title: Google puts users at risk by downplaying health disclaimers under AI Overviews

summary: In January 2026, a Guardian investigation found Google AI Overviews at the top of health-search results giving inaccurate or misleading medical information. Examples included telling people with pancreatic cancer to avoid high-fat food, presenting liver-test reference numbers without patient context, and confusing cervical screening with vaginal-cancer testing; specialist charities described the potential for missed care or compromised treatment. Google disputed the breadth of the examples and said many summaries cited reputable sources and advised professional help. It removed AI Overviews for two liver-test queries after the report, but query variants and other criticised summaries still appeared. A February follow-up found that the general medical caution was absent from the initial summary and appeared only after “Show more,” beneath extra advice in less prominent text. No specific patient decision or clinical injury is established.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: The Guardian independently tested multiple AI Overview health queries and sought specialist review: a pancreatic cancer result advised avoiding high-fat foods contrary to specialist guidance; liver-function ranges lacked essential clinical context; a vaginal-cancer result misidentified a cervical pap test. The article documents results on a prominent answer surface and risk estimates from health charities, not actual patient injury. Google said examples were often incomplete screenshots, cited reputable sources, and its internal clinicians disputed some inaccuracies. By 11 January, the liver-test summaries for two exact queries had been removed, while variants and other health outputs remained, according to the Guardian. On 16 February, the same reporter tested the interface and found a general medical disclaimer only after expanding “Show more” and scrolling past additional advice; Google said its summaries often directly urged medical help when appropriate and did not deny the reported disclaimer position. AIAAIC indexes the case, but is not independent observation of every output. The complete live query-response set, exposure count, clinical decisions and injury outcomes are unavailable.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: A low-assurance synthesis acquired prominent Search-answer authority on consequential health questions. Independently, the general medical caution existed but was placed beyond the initial answer and below expanded advice, so it did not reach the user at the first point of likely reliance. The reported exact-query removals reduced some exposure without establishing that neighbouring queries or the broader warning path were repaired. The tested direct-answer assurance failure and late caution delivery remain distinct from patient injury, which is not established. The warning clause remains partly unresolved on activation/effect conditions. Narrow removals do not prove broader recovery. Benchmark, detector, model-development and voluntary programme scope remain independently bounded.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: The case separates answer correctness from delivery of its caution. A warning technically present at the bottom of an expanded panel cannot be assumed to govern a decision made from the initial summary; subsequent exact-query removal also must not be mistaken for a general fix.
